project.name: Lua
project.vulnerable_commit_evidence: The staged repository under `gt_results/arvo_31541/_work/src/lua` resolves local Git `HEAD` to `c03c527fd207b4ad8f5a8e0f4f2c176bd227c979`; this trace is grounded in that staged checkout rather than an inferred ancestor.

bug_description.original: A security vulnerability exists where tail calls are not handled by 'luaD_precall' in the same way as regular calls, leading to code duplication and potential inconsistencies in call handling.
bug_description.normalized: The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `c0ed74c1e130aa6d80e5ffc7b6e32b433aca1765`, while the staged repository snapshot used in this result is the checkout under `gt_results/arvo_31541/_work/src/lua`, whose local Git metadata resolves `HEAD` to `c03c527fd207b4ad8f5a8e0f4f2c176bd227c979`; the trace below is grounded in that staged source snapshot, the staged patch, and Stage 01's saved ASan crash. The exact 593-byte Lua text witness is first materialized in `luaL_loadbufferx()` as `LoadS ls`, then wrapped in `ZIO z` and parsed into the `Proto` and `lineinfo` state later executed by `luaV_execute()`. During `OP_TAILCALL`, vulnerable `luaD_pretailcall()` copies the callee closure and arguments into the reused caller frame before `checkstackGC()`/`luaD_growstack()` can still raise `stack overflow`, so `ci->func` already names the callee `Proto` while `ci->u.l.savedpc` still names the caller instruction because `ci->u.l.savedpc = p->code` at `ldo.c:480` is never reached. `luaG_runerror()` then asks `getcurrentline(ci)` for source information, `currentpc()` subtracts the callee `p->code` from the caller `savedpc`, and `luaG_getfuncline()` walks past a 21-byte `lineinfo` allocation at `ldebug.c:88`. The patch removes `luaD_pretailcall()` and moves frame relocation into `luaD_precall()` only after the stack check succeeds; Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

tainted_value_origin.description: The libFuzzer harness feeds the exact staged 593-byte witness directly into `luaL_loadbufferx()` in text mode (`"t"`), so the same attacker-controlled bytes become the Lua source later parsed into the `Proto` and `lineinfo` state used by the vulnerable tail-call error path.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker buffer. `luaL_loadbufferx()` stores the raw pointer and exact length into `LoadS ls`, the reader state that `getS()` later exposes to the parser through `lua_load()` and `ZIO`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_31541/poc` has sha256 `33e71dcf393d14020cc63b77186802e84ee93be6ec3d8a171cf68bdd55e50154` and size 593 bytes. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` passes those exact `data,size` arguments into `luaL_loadbufferx(L, data, size, "test", "t")`, so `buff` and `size` here are the same file bytes and extent when `LoadS ls` is initialized.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable tail-call helper overwrites the reused caller frame with the callee closure and arguments before the later `checkstackGC(L, fsize)` can still raise. On that error path, `ci->func` already names the callee while `ci->u.l.savedpc` still names the caller instruction.
root_cause.note: The fix removes `luaD_pretailcall()` and moves this parameter relocation into `luaD_precall()` only after `checkstackGCp()` succeeds, precisely to keep debug information consistent when an error is raised before the new function starts.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `luaG_getfuncline()` walks the callee `Proto`'s `lineinfo` array with an out-of-range `pc` derived from the mismatched `CallInfo`, so this load reads past the 21-byte heap allocation created for that `lineinfo` vector.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` at `ldebug.c:88:19` with stack `luaG_getfuncline -> getcurrentline -> luaG_runerror -> luaD_growstack -> luaD_pretailcall` and says the access lands 10 bytes to the right of a 21-byte region allocated by `close_func()`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved vulnerable run reaches `docall()` and then `luaV_execute()`, so `luaD_protectedparser()` accepted the exact staged text chunk here and left a Lua closure on the stack for execution.

fine_trace.note: The harness feeds the exact staged witness file (593 bytes, sha256 `33e71dcf393d14020cc63b77186802e84ee93be6ec3d8a171cf68bdd55e50154`) into `luaL_loadbufferx()` with mode `"t"`, so the buffer is parsed strictly as Lua source text before execution.

Source. `luaL_loadbufferx()` materializes the attacker-controlled buffer pointer and exact length into `LoadS ls`, creating the project-side reader state that later hands the same bytes to the parser.
The freshly initialized `LoadS` object is passed to `lua_load()` together with reader callback `getS`, preserving both the witness pointer and its size as the parser input object.
`lua_load()` stores `reader = getS` and `data = &ls` inside `ZIO z`, so later parser reads will pull bytes from the same `LoadS` state produced in steps 2 and 3.

`luaD_protectedparser()` is the first parser call that consumes the witness-backed `ZIO` and builds the closure/`Proto` tree whose bytecode and debug tables later reach the vulnerable tail-call error path.

When the parser closes one of the witness-created Lua functions, it shrinks that function's debug line table to exactly `fs->pc` entries. ASan later identifies the overread object as a 21-byte heap region allocated through this call chain, so this is the `Proto->lineinfo` extent later consumed at the sink.

fine_trace.code: savepc(ci);  /* several calls here can raise errors */
fine_trace.note: Inside `OP_TAILCALL`, the interpreter snapshots the caller's current program counter into `ci->u.l.savedpc` before any helper that can error. On the same VM path the target at `ra` is treated as a Lua closure, so execution will enter `luaD_pretailcall()` instead of the `!ttisLclosure(s2v(ra))` C-function branch.

Root cause. `luaD_pretailcall()` reuses the caller frame and copies the callee closure plus arguments into `ci->func + i` before it has proved that entering the callee cannot raise. After this loop, `ci->func` points at the callee's stack slot contents while the caller `savedpc` from step 7 is still intact.

The stack-space check runs only after the frame rewrite in step 8. On the reproducing run it falls into `luaD_growstack()` and raises `stack overflow`; because the error happens here, line 480 (`ci->u.l.savedpc = p->code`) is never reached, so the partially rewritten `CallInfo` still pairs callee `ci->func` with caller `savedpc`.
Handling the stack-overflow error, `luaG_runerror()` asks the current Lua frame for source and line information. It therefore consumes the inconsistent `CallInfo` state left by steps 8 and 9.

`currentpc()` derives the instruction index by subtracting `ci_func(ci)->p->code` from `ci->u.l.savedpc`. After steps 8 and 9, those fields refer to different functions: `ci_func(ci)->p` is the callee `Proto` now exposed through `ci->func`, but `savedpc` still belongs to the caller, so the resulting `pc` is out of range for the callee's debug tables.

Sink. `luaG_getfuncline()` uses the out-of-range `pc` from step 11 to walk `f->lineinfo`. The relevant `lineinfo` buffer is one of the parser-created tables from step 6, and ASan reports this load as a `heap-buffer-overflow` read at line 88 that lands 10 bytes past a 21-byte heap region allocated by `close_func()`.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 10 bytes to the right of a 21-byte region allocated through `luaM_shrinkvector_()` from this call site.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from the staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` (the primary Stage 01 crash artifact, which reports READ size 16) and `reproduction_report.json`; `default_crash_trace.txt` shows the same source location and stack with a smaller optimized read, and the fixed image was not dynamically validated in Stage 02.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack shows `close_func()` shrinking a `Proto->lineinfo` buffer. Step 6 and steps 11-12 explain how the tail-call error path later uses a `pc` computed against the wrong `Proto` and walks past that same debug table.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_31541 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which ran the staged witness in the vulnerable ARVO workspace and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with stack `luaG_getfuncline -> getcurrentline -> luaG_runerror -> luaD_growstack -> luaD_pretailcall`.

format.name: Exact staged Lua text witness that reaches the vulnerable tail-call stack-overflow path
format.contract: Exactly the 593-byte file `gt_results/arvo_31541/poc` with sha256 `33e71dcf393d14020cc63b77186802e84ee93be6ec3d8a171cf68bdd55e50154`, loaded by `luaL_loadbufferx(..., "test", "t")` as Lua source text. On the observed vulnerable run, those exact bytes parse successfully, execute to `luaV_execute()`'s `OP_TAILCALL` path for a Lua closure, and make `luaD_pretailcall()` call into `luaD_growstack()` before error reporting overreads a 21-byte `Proto->lineinfo` table in `luaG_getfuncline()`. The saved artifacts do not justify any broader claim about other Lua scripts, nearby text mutations, or other tail-call shapes.
